key_insight: Reward-Forcing introduces a reward-based feedback loop for autoregressive video generators that reduces reliance on teacher models and brings output quality closer to bidirectional counterparts, enabling higher-quality near real-time generation.
problem_solved: Autoregressive video generation frequently depends on strong teacher models and lags behind bidirectional architectures in output quality; this paper addresses how to train autoregressive models to achieve competitive quality without heavy teacher supervision.
method: Propose a Reward-Forcing training objective that supplies scalar/structured reward feedback to the autoregressive decoder instead of relying solely on a teacher model.
Use a learned reward function and/or perceptual metrics to evaluate generated frames/sequences and backpropagate guidance that improves temporal coherence and visual fidelity.
Integrate the reward feedback into the autoregressive sampling loop so the model refines next-frame predictions and reduces dependence on a separate teacher model.
impact: Makes high-quality, low-latency autoregressive video generation more practical by decreasing dependence on strong teacher models—beneficial for real-time applications, deployment, and interactive generative systems.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: autoregressive generator + reward module with a feedback arrow (training loop).
Training flowchart: how rewards are computed (learned metric / perceptual score) and used to update the autoregressive model.
Metric comparison chart: quality vs latency for Reward-Forcing, teacher-based autoregressive, and bidirectional baselines.
Sample timelines: frame sequences showing improved temporal coherence and visual fidelity with reward feedback.
paper_title: Reward-Forcing: Autoregressive Video Generation with Reward Feedback
paper_authors: Jingran Zhang, Ning Li, Yuanhao Ban, Andrew Bai, Justin Cui
